BUS.G11.T3.MARKETING.A1.title: The marketing function
BUS.G11.T3.MARKETING.A1.description: Aspects of the marketing function: marketing activities, product policy (development, design, packaging, trademarks), pricing policy, distribution policy (channels, intermediaries, direct/indirect), communication policy (advertising, sales promotion, publicity, personal selling) and foreign marketing (imports and exports).
BUS.G11.T3.MARKETING.A1.strand: T3 — Entrepreneurial success, citizenship, marketing & production functions
BUS.G11.T3.MARKETING.A1.recovery_strategy: Tie each activity to its marketing policy: product = design, packaging and brand; pricing = setting the price; distribution = getting it to the customer (channels, intermediaries); communication = telling customers about it (advertising, selling). Foreign marketing = imports and exports.

questions.question: The four Ps of the marketing mix are product, price, place and _________.
questions.expected: promotion
questions.memo: The four Ps are product, price, place (distribution) and promotion (marketing communication).

questions.question: Which marketing policy covers a product's design, packaging and branding?
questions.expected: Product policy
questions.memo: Product policy deals with the product itself — its development, design, packaging and trademark.

questions.question: True or false: Advertising is part of marketing communication.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Advertising is one form of marketing communication, used to tell customers about a product.

questions.question: Distribution (place) is mainly about:
options: Getting the product to the customer
questions.expected: Getting the product to the customer
questions.memo: Distribution is about the channels and intermediaries that move the product from the producer to the customer.

questions.question: Selling goods to customers in other countries is called _________.
questions.expected: exporting
questions.memo: Exporting is selling goods to other countries; importing is buying goods from other countries.

questions.question: True or false: Pricing policy decides how much to charge for a product.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Pricing policy sets the price, using factors such as cost, demand and competition.

questions.question: Sort each activity under the marketing policy it belongs to.

items.text: Setting a discount for bulk buyers
Choosing wholesalers to carry the product

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Packaging and design = product; discounts and price = pricing; wholesalers = distribution; adverts = communication.

questions.question: What is an intermediary in distribution?
options: A middleman, such as a wholesaler or retailer, between producer and consumer
The factory that makes the product
The final customer who uses the product
questions.expected: A middleman, such as a wholesaler or retailer, between producer and consumer
questions.memo: Intermediaries — wholesalers and retailers — sit between the producer and the consumer and help move the product along.

questions.question: Read the case and select the marketing COMMUNICATION (promotion) activities.
questions.source_text: To launch its new juice, a company redesigned the bottle and lowered the price for the first month. It also ran television adverts and offered free samples in supermarkets, while signing a deal with a national chain of stores to stock it.
questions.task: Tap the parts that are marketing communication (promotion) activities.

targets.reason: Free samples are a sales-promotion (communication) activity.

questions.expected: ran television adverts; offered free samples in supermarkets
questions.memo: TV adverts and free samples are communication/promotion. Redesigning the bottle is product, lowering the price is pricing, and the store deal is distribution.

questions.question: _________ marketing involves selling to and buying from other countries through exports and imports.
questions.expected: Foreign
questions.memo: Foreign marketing deals with trade across borders — exporting goods abroad and importing goods from abroad.

questions.question: What is the difference between direct and indirect distribution?
options: Direct sells straight to the customer; indirect uses intermediaries like wholesalers
Direct uses many middlemen; indirect uses none
Direct is always cheaper for the customer
There is no difference between them
questions.expected: Direct sells straight to the customer; indirect uses intermediaries like wholesalers
questions.memo: Direct distribution goes straight from producer to customer; indirect distribution passes through intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers.

questions.question: True or false: Packaging both protects the product and helps to market it.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Good packaging protects the product and also attracts customers and carries the brand, so it is part of product policy.

questions.question: Sort each example into direct or indirect distribution.

items.text: A farmer selling vegetables at their own farm stall
A factory selling through wholesalers and shops
A baker selling directly from their shopfront
A producer using a chain of retailers
An online store shipping straight to the buyer
A manufacturer supplying a supermarket group

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Selling straight to the customer is direct; using wholesalers or retailers in between is indirect.

questions.question: Which of these is a factor that influences a product's price?
options: The cost of making it, demand, and competitors' prices
The colour of the owner's car
The day of the week the owner was born
The number of letters in the brand name
questions.expected: The cost of making it, demand, and competitors' prices
questions.memo: Pricing is influenced by production cost, customer demand and what competitors charge.

questions.question: What is personal selling?
options: A salesperson dealing directly with a customer to make a sale
Printing posters with no human contact
questions.expected: A salesperson dealing directly with a customer to make a sale
questions.memo: Personal selling is face-to-face (or direct) contact between a salesperson and a customer, a form of marketing communication.

questions.question: Read the case and select the DISTRIBUTION (place) decisions.
questions.source_text: A shoe brand improved its leather quality and set a premium price. It then appointed regional wholesalers and opened branded outlets in three cities, while filming a glossy advert for social media.
questions.task: Tap the parts that are distribution (place) decisions.

targets.reason: Using wholesalers is a distribution decision.

targets.phrase: opened branded outlets in three cities
targets.reason: Opening outlets is about getting the product to customers — distribution.

questions.expected: appointed regional wholesalers; opened branded outlets in three cities
questions.memo: Wholesalers and outlets are distribution. Improving leather is product, the premium price is pricing, and the advert is communication.

questions.question: Sales of a good product are slow because few people know it exists. Which marketing policy most needs attention?
options: Communication (promotion) — to make customers aware of it
Product — the product is the problem
questions.expected: Communication (promotion) — to make customers aware of it
questions.memo: If a good product is simply not known, the gap is in communication/promotion, which builds awareness.

questions.question: How does effective marketing help a business achieve its objectives?
options: It attracts and keeps customers, driving sales and income towards the business's goals
It only adds costs with no benefit
It replaces the need to make a good product
It guarantees the business never competes
questions.expected: It attracts and keeps customers, driving sales and income towards the business's goals
questions.memo: Marketing brings in and retains customers, generating the sales and income a business needs to meet its objectives.

questions.question: Why must foreign marketing be aligned with the production function?
options: Production must be able to meet export demand with the right quantity and quality
Foreign marketing has nothing to do with production
Exports never affect how much is produced
questions.expected: Production must be able to meet export demand with the right quantity and quality
questions.memo: Winning export orders is pointless if production cannot supply the right quantity and quality on time, so the two functions must align.

questions.question: A new premium snack is well-made but priced the same as cheap rivals and sold only at a remote farm stall. Which combination of fixes fits the marketing mix?
options: Set a price that reflects its quality and widen distribution to reach more customers
Lower the quality to match the price
questions.expected: Set a price that reflects its quality and widen distribution to reach more customers
questions.memo: A premium product needs a matching price (pricing) and broader distribution (place) so the right customers can find and buy it.
